summary.text: Herald of Agamemnon, sent with Talthybius to fetch Briseis from Achilles — and the Ithacan attendant who gathered up Odysseus' cloak when Athena set him running to still the assembly.

story.text: He and Talthybius were Agamemnon's heralds and ready squires. At the king's command they went unwilling to Achilles' hut to lead away fair-cheeked Briseis — the errand that sealed the hero's withdrawal from the war.

When Athena roused Odysseus to face the mutinous host, he cast off his cloak and ran; Eurybates of Ithaca, who waited on him, gathered it up. So the same man serves both the commander of the army and the prince of Ithaca — herald's office binding king to counsellor.
In the embassy of Book 9 he attends Odysseus among the heralds sent to Achilles' tent, bearing the king's offer of gifts and the return of Briseis.
